//: HOW THIS APP GETS BUILT. Read EAS-BUILD.md next to this file first.
NOTHING HERE HAS EVER BEEN RUN. This app has only ever been opened in
Expo Go. No native binary of it exists, no credentials have been
generated, and no build has been paid for. This file is the
configuration for a first build, not a record of one.
NO SECRETS IN THIS FILE, EVER. The repository is PUBLIC. Every value a
build needs that is not in here goes into EAS environment variables
(`eas env:create`), which is also the only way a cloud builder can see
them at all — it does not read the laptop's .env.
THE `env` BLOCKS BELOW CARRY ONLY SWITCHES, never an address and never a
key. EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE, EXPO_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY,
EXPO_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_TERMS_URL are all set as EAS
environment variables per environment. The two legal URLs are a
SUBMISSION BLOCKER: without them the app draws no policy links and
App Review fails on guideline 5.1.1.
`appVersionSource: remote` means EAS owns the build number and bumps it
itself. `version` in app.json stays the marketing version and is the
owner's to change; the build number underneath it is not something
anybody should be editing by hand between submissions.
A DEV CLIENT ON A REAL DEVICE. This is the profile that replaces Expo
Go, and running it once is how the surprises listed in EAS-BUILD.md
get found before a store submission rather than after one.
It needs a registered device UDID (`eas device:create`).
THE RELEASE BUILD, WITHOUT THE STORE. Same code path as production —
a real Release binary, no dev client, no bundler — installed straight
onto registered devices via TestFlight or an internal link.
THIS IS THE PROFILE TO BUILD FIRST. It is what proves push
notifications, permission prompts and deep links behave outside Expo
Go, and finding a problem here costs a rebuild instead of a rejected
submission and a week.
WHAT GOES TO THE APP STORE. `autoIncrement` bumps the build number so
a resubmission after a rejection cannot collide with the one before
it — App Store Connect refuses a duplicate build number, and doing it
by hand is how that gets forgotten under pressure.
EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_TOOLS and EXPO_PUBLIC_FIXTURES are pinned OFF here
rather than merely left unset. Fixtures mode renders sample balances
and sample alerts that look exactly like real ones; shipping it on by
accident would put fabricated data in front of a reviewer, which is
the one thing this app is built never to do.
DELIBERATELY EMPTY, AND IT MUST STAY THAT WAY IN THIS REPOSITORY.
`eas submit` wants three values here: appleId (the Apple ID email),
ascAppId (the numeric App Store Connect app id, created when the
app record is made) and appleTeamId. NONE OF THEM EXIST YET — there
is no confirmed Apple Developer account, so there is no team id and
no app record.
They are also not values to commit to a public repository. Set them
as EAS environment variables and reference them, or pass them on the
command line at submit time. `eas submit` will otherwise prompt for
each one interactively, which is a perfectly good answer for a first
submission.
